cells.tense: You have chosen a direction, and the whole pattern holds it now.
cells.act: hold someone else up with what you have
cells.ask: Give someone moving your way one real piece of what you know how to do — a clear piece, finished, nothing owed back — and leave the choice you made standing as it is.
cells.core:
You're pointed, and it's not logic doing the pointing — it's a call you can see, plain as daylight. From this ridge the whole pattern shows, and what makes it land is that people near you get your strength without having to ask twice. Your direction stays yours and it feeds whoever's in range; that's the shape when it's working.

It only holds while you're actually done choosing. The picture stays steady because the choice stays made — quiet, no announcements — and the strength reaches others because you don't hide it. So aim that outward once. Your direction doesn't need defending out here. You already picked it, and the picking is the work.
cells.sheetLine: The choice is made, and it holds.
cells.verb: steering by a direction you chose
cells.place: on the ridge where the whole pattern shows in one look

cells.tense: You will have turned this toward something else before it has settled.
cells.act: list the pulls on you and mark which are yours
cells.ask: Name what's tugging at you and mark which of those are yours, then take one marked line forward and leave the rest quiet while it settles.
cells.core:
The aim is already set, and you're treating it as unfinished. Names get drafted, the pitch rehearsed, the whole pattern re-read in case a better direction is hiding inside it — all of it ahead of what's next, instead of the ground you already picked. The picture gets called richer each time you go back to it, and going back to it gets in the way of the walking.

Nothing new is needed. What you're calling doubt is supply — you hold so many true things that one plain direction can't sit alone. So set the pulls side by side and mark which ones are yours, one at a time. Then take one forward and leave the rest quiet. Let them have weight without being obeyed. A direction acts now; it doesn't get argued with all the way to the end.
cells.sheetLine: The turning is getting sketched, not finished.

cells.tense: You kept the old direction and stayed with it after the others moved on.
cells.ask: Sit ten unhurried minutes with something you actually made or grew, and find what it gives you to enjoy. Leave the old direction alone for the week.
cells.core:
You steered by a direction and you're still where it left you. Others moved, the sky turned, and you stayed with the call that was yours when you made it. Nothing in you points anywhere now — what you built is like a field after the harvest. There's nothing to push into, and pushing wouldn't get you anywhere.

Not every direction stays worth the walking. Some were for a season. So look at what you actually made while you chased it — one thing you grew. Take ten unhurried minutes with it and see what it gives you to enjoy. Rest in it; don't argue for it. Then put some time between you and that old heading. Noticing works on the calendar, not in a rush.

cells.tense: You are holding people up while calling it just how you are, pen down.
cells.act: share your strength where it is needed
cells.ask: Next time you catch yourself carrying someone's weight, stay with it a minute and name it plainly to yourself as something you chose. Then keep at it or stop — both are open.
cells.core:
You hold people up. When someone's floundering you step in, share what you have, keep them standing, and afterwards you'd say you didn't do anything special — that's just what people do. The strength going out is real. The hand on it is yours, and you don't count it as yours.

That strength doesn't need defending or announcing; it needs crediting, to you, once. The next time you're carrying someone's weight, stay with the moment long enough to know you decided to. Then keep at it or don't — either's honest. A steward sees the grip; yours goes unseen, and unseen strength wears a person before they notice. Name it, once, and the account is square.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the Too Little cell can know what ended: the record says 'past-anchored, still standing at a door already behind' but not what the door was, so the draft must say only that others moved and this person stayed with the earlier calling — no event, no person, no duration, no cost. A reader could reasonably say 'I am still moving toward something,' in which case the ask survives because enjoying one tended thing costs nothing and teaches them anyway. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any line that sounds final about the old star — a clean, conclusive image of an ending reads beautifully and tells them their life, so it comes out. Too Much and Too Little are the same failure and its opposite: one aims faster than the direction exists, the other keeps the old star after the sky changed.
